title: Proportional slot shepherding and attention-priority decay for tail mitigation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We continue to see sporadic p95/p99 latency spikes when small high-priority prefills (short prompts with heavy attention patterns) interleave with long-running decode requests on heterogenous kernels. Current admission and batch-shaping strategies allocate slots greedily or by coarse priority buckets, which leads to kernel mismatch, inefficient cache usage, and straggling tokens during tail events.

Proposal summary: Implement a proportional slot shepherding mechanism in the admission controller paired with an attention-priority decay signal. The admission controller will: 1) maintain lightweight per-tenant (or per-route) soft quotas expressed in token-slot units, 2) compute a short-term urgency score for each incoming prefill/stream based on remaining deadline, observed attention density, and historical kernel affinity, and 3) allocate or probabilistically relinquish reserved slots proportionally, allowing short urgent requests to preempt fractionally while avoiding global starvation.

The attention-priority decay signal decays urgency for long-running decodes that show low attention reuse (low KV cache hit-rate) so that kernel affinity decisions can migrate those decodes to lower-cost kernels or bump them into background batch lanes. We will also propagate kernel_hint metadata earlier (at admission time) to the kernel-selection layer so preferred kernels can be queued in parallel instead of waiting until decode handoff.

Why this is different: Instead of hard priority buckets or strict preemption, proportional shepherding allows controlled, probabilistic relinquish behavior that smooths tail events without thundering preemptions. Combining that with an attention-aware decay reduces cache-thrashing and helps the kernel selector to choose an execution path that matches long-run characteristics.

Scope/what we'll deliver in this ticket:
- Admission controller changes: soft quota bookkeeping, urgency scoring, probabilistic relinquish policy, metrics emission.
- Attention-priority decay estimator: lightweight online estimator of attention density and KV hit-rate, exposing decay weight.
- Early kernel_hint propagation: attach kernel affinity hints to admission tokens and expose a small early-queue for kernel scheduler to pre-warm candidate kernels.
- Safety and rollout: feature flag gate, canary rollout by route, A/B comparisons, rollback path.

Performance targets (goal):
- Reduce p99 decode tail latency by >= 20% on sampled customer workloads with mixed prompt lengths.
- Reduce incidence of kernel mismatch handoffs by >= 30% for affected workloads.
- Maintain or improve median latency and keep unit cost delta <= +3% for steady-state traffic.

Out-of-scope: full redesign of kernel scheduler internals, global admission-rewrite for Dedicated autoscaling, or changes to client-facing APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Implemented proportional slot shepherding in the admission controller behind a feature flag
Attention-priority decay estimator running in production canary with emitted metrics (attention_density, kv_hit_rate, decay_weight)
Kernel_hint metadata is attached at admission time and consumed by kernel scheduler prewarm path in canary agents
End-to-end canary demonstrates >=20% p99 reduction on internal mixed-length replay test and no regression on median latency
Dashboard exposing new metrics and an automated alert if unit-cost increases by >5% during rollout
Design doc and implementation PRs reviewed and merged; rollout plan executed with ability to rollback within 30 minutes
implementation_plan: Proto: add urgency_score computation in admission path (Maya) — initial bench against replay traces
Engine: implement soft quota table and probabilistic relinquish (Anders) — unit tests + race detector
Estimator: integrate attention_density and kv_hit_rate counters in prefill pipeline (Eng intern) — expose via metrics/trace
Kernel: wire kernel_hint metadata to scheduler prewarm API — small protocol bump (backwards-compatible)
Canary: create canary route and traffic shaping to run A/B for 24h with dashboards
Rollout: staged increase to 25%/50%/100% across routes with automated rollback conditions
risks_and_mitigations: Race conditions in soft quota bookkeeping under high-concurrency — mitigation: use sharded atomics and strong unit tests; start with coarse-grained LRU eviction
Over-aggressive relinquish causes throughput drop — mitigation: conservative default probability and canary experiment; expose tuning knobs
Estimator misclassifies attention-heavy short bursts as low-priority — mitigation: keep decay time constants configurable and tuned by offline replay
Kernel_hint misrouting increases cold-starts — mitigation: prewarm budget and fallbacks to current selection; monitor kernel mismatch rate closely
metrics_to_track: p50/p95/p99 decode latency by route and kernel
steady-state throughput and unit_cost (tokens/sec and $/1M tokens)

2025-11-30 - Load test: Internal 48h run shows kernel_mismatch_rate down 37% and p99 down 22% in canary, but unit_cost increased by 4.2% under highly-interleaved synthetic workload. Plan: tune relinquish_probability and decay constants.
